q: Clinical history is suggestive of premature ejaculation in male, with history of relationship conflicts with wife. Non pharmacological treatment for the couple used in this condition?
e:
A. Squeeze therapy
Explanation
Squeeze therapy is a behavioral technique specifically designed to help men with premature ejaculation. It involves the partner squeezing the penis just below the glans at the moment the man feels he is about to ejaculate, delaying ejaculation and helping the individual gain control.

Other options:
B. Sensate focus technique is a form of sex therapy aimed at reducing performance anxiety and improving intimacy but is not specific for premature ejaculation C. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is useful for addressing psychological factors like anxiety or stress but is not the first-line intervention for premature ejaculation D. Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is used primarily in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and is not relevant for premature ejaculation management.

q: History of chronic alcohol abuse now presented with acute onset confusion, 6th nerve palsy, gaze palsy, ataxia. Likely diagnosis?
e:
A. Wernicke’s encephalopathy
Explanation
Wernicke encephalopathy is an acute neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency, commonly seen in chronic alcoholics. It is characterized by the classic triad of confusion, ophthalmoplegia (e.g., gaze palsy, sixth nerve palsy), and ataxia

Other options:
B. Korsakoff psychosis is a chronic condition that often follows untreated Wernicke encephalopathy and is associated with severe memory deficits and confabulation but does not present with acute ophthalmoplegia or ataxia C. Delirium tremens is a withdrawal syndrome seen in alcoholics that involves severe agitation, hallucinations, and autonomic hyperactivity, but it does not include ophthalmoplegia or ataxia D. De Clérambault syndrome is a delusional disorder where the individual believes another person is in love with them

q: A 32 year old female presented with heavy hairloss since few months. She gives history of suffering with COVID 19 eight month back. What is the likely diagnosis?
e:
A. Telogen effluvium
Explanation
Option A-This is a case of Telogen effluvium,which is a common type of hair loss that affects people after they experience severe stress or a change to their body. Symptoms include thinning hair, usually around the top of your head. Treatment exists to reverse hair loss, but hair will typically grow back in three to six months without treatment. Option B-Female pattern hair loss leads to central balding,but there will be no history of stressor like fever. Option C-Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease that attacks your body’s hair follicles, causing patchy hair loss.It will be a well circumscribed patch with no erythema or inflammation.Again,there will be no history of stressor like fever. Option D-Trichotillomania is when someone cannot resist the urge to pull out their hair. They may pull out the hair on their head or in other places, such as their eyebrows or eyelashes.It can present with tonsure sign.

q: A farmer having trauma in lower limb following which a cauliflower like growth developed on that site. On HPE Copper penny bodies are seen. What is the diagnosis?
e:
A. Chromoblastomycosis
Explanation
Option A-Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic fungal infection of the skin and the subcutaneous tissue caused by traumatic inoculation of a specific group of dematiaceous fungi (usually Fonsecaea pedrosoi, Phialophora verrucosa). The patient presents with cauliflower like growth.On HPE, Copper penny bodies are seen. Option B-Mycetoma is characterised by sinuses,swelling and sulphur granules. Option C-Asteroid bodies are star-shaped inclusions seen in Sporotrichosis. Option D-Phaeohyphomycosis can be caused by many species of dark, melanin-pigmented dematiaceous fungi including Bipolaris, Cladophialophora etc.

q: This appearance is seen in ?
e:
A. Vitamin A deficiency
Explanation
Option A-Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) can cause a range of ocular manifestations, known collectively as xerophthalmia , including night blindness, conjunctival and corneal xerosis, and keratomalacia.The given image shows Bitot’s spots,which are typically dry-appearing triangular patches of xerosed conjunctiva with a layer of foam on the surface, usually located temporal to the cornea. Option B-Vitamin B3 deficiency i.e,niacin deficiency can present with casal's necklace. Option C-Vitamin B12 deficiency presents with hyperpigmented knuckles.

q: There is a 0.3 cm ulcerated nodule on nasolabial fold. Diagnosis is ?
e:
A. Basal cell carcinoma
Explanation
Option A-Basal cell carcinoma can present as a shiny, skin-colored bump that's translucent, meaning you can see a bit through the surface. The bump can look pearly white or pink on white skin.It can also present as ulcerated nodule on nasolabial fold with in a burrowing in appearance known as rodent ulcer. Option B-Most melanomas are brown and black, but they can also be pink, tan, or white. Option C-Squamous cell carcinoma has everted edges. Option D-Kaposi Sarcoma presents as cancerous lesions (spots) on the skin that are purple, red or brown and can appear flat or raised.

q: A patient presented with nail pitting, subungual hyperkeratosis and following nail feature. Diagnosis is?
e:
A. Psoriasis
Explanation
Option A-The given image shows oil drop sign/salmon patch appearance on nail bed which is pathognomonic of psoriasis.Other features of psoriasis are irregular nail pitting, subungual hyperkeratosis and onycholysis. Option B-Lichen planus presents with longitudinal ridging and fissuring, nail plate thinning, and trachyonychia. Option C-Alopecia areata causes regular pitting on nails known as geometric pitting.

q: A female with BMI-30kg/m2 presented with following picture. This is associated with?
e:
A. Metabolic syndrome
Explanation
Option A-Acanthosis nigricans is a condition that causes areas of dark, thick velvety skin in body folds and creases. It typically affects the armpits, groin and neck. Acanthosis nigricans tends to affect people with obesity.hence,it is seen in metabolic syndrome. Option B-Addison’s disease can present with dark hyperpigmented gums and palmar creases. Option C-Hypothyroidism is often associated with vitiligo. Option D-Parathyroid disease can cause metastatic calcification in skin.

q: A Patient presented with borderline leprosy of the face.which nerve is affected?
e:
B. CN7
Explanation
The most common cranial nerve affected in leprosy is facial nerve>trigeminal nerve. Hence,CN7 is a better answer than CN5.

q: A truck driver comes with complaints of painless, indurated genital ulcer after unprotected/unsafe intercourse. The motility of the causative agent can be detected by which type of microscope
e:
A. Dark field microscope
Explanation
Option A-The given case scenario of painless, indurated genital ulcer after unprotected/unsafe intercourse suggests the diagnosis of syphilis.The motility of the causative agent i.e,treponema pallidum can be detected by Dark field microscope. q: A patient presented with finger with paronychia & extensive linear wheal like pattern on upper limb. Antibiotic for treatment?
e:
A. Amoxiclav
Explanation
Option A-The given case scenario of finger with paronychia & extensive linear wheal like pattern on upper limb suggests the diagnosis of cellulitis.The most common organism is staphylococcus aureus.Amoxiclav is the drug of choice in cellulitis. Option B,C,D-Norfloxacin,Amikacin and Metronidazole are not the first line for cellulitis.

q: A migrant labourer presented with burning micturition and urethral discharge within one week of unprotected sexual intercourse. What is the causative agent?
e:
B. Gonorrhoea
Explanation
Option A,C,D-E.coli,Ureaplasma and Trichomonas are less common causes of urethritis following sexual intercourse and the incubation period is usually more than 1 week. Option B-since patient presented with burning micturition and urethral discharge,it indicates diagnosis of urethritis.And since the patient was symptomatic within one week of unprotected sexual intercourse.The causative agent will be neisseria gonorrhea.

q: A married female infertile for 4 years want to conceive complaints of profuse non-foul smelling, non itchy white discharge for 2 days. Her last menstrual period was 13-14 days back. Diagnosis?
e:
B. Physiological
Explanation
Option A-Candidiasis is a vaginal yeast infection which may cause intense itching of the vagina and vulva, and women often have a thick, white, curd-like discharge. Option B-Physiological discharge is profuse, non-foul smelling, non itchy and white in colour and it especially occurs around the day of ovulation i.e. 14th day of menstrual cycle. Option C-Bacterial vaginosis shows profuse,off white discharge with foul smell. Option D-Trichomoniasis shows greenish frothy discharge.

q: A 30 year old patient comes with flaccid bullae on the skin which is easy to rupture. Biopsy revealed suprabasal split. What is the diagnosis?
e:
A. Pemphigus vulgaris

q: A patient who is a farmer works in maize field and have more maize in his food presented with diarrhoea, dementia and some lesions on neck, which vitamin deficiency can lead to the given condition?

A. Niacin
Explanation

Option B-Riboflavin deficiency presents with cheilitis,glossitis and angular stomatitis. Option C-Pyridoxine deficiency presents with peripheral neuropathy. Option D-Tyrosine deficiency cannot lead to niacin deficiency.Tryptophan deficiency can lead to niacin deficiency.

q: A girl child presented with rough keratotic lesions over her elbow, knee and she also had problem in dark vision/night vision. Diagnosis?
e:
A. Phrynoderma
Explanation
Option A-Phrynoderma is a form of asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic follicular hyperkeratosis, where follicular papules of various sizes are found on the back of the elbows and the front of the knees, and can spread to involve the extremities, upper forearms and thighs.This is seen in cases of vitamin A deficieny,essential fatty acid deficiency and malnutrition. Option B-KP(keratosis pilaris) is a harmless skin condition that causes dry, rough patches and tiny bumps, often on the upper arms, thighs, cheeks or buttocks. The bumps usually don't hurt or itch. Option C-Darier disease, previously known as keratosis follicularis, is a genodermatosis inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion.This rare disease classically features multiple red or brown papules with hyperkeratosis and nail abnormalities (eg, longitudinal erythronychia). Option D-Folliculitis is a common skin condition that happens when hair follicles become inflamed. It's often caused by an infection with bacteria. At first it may look like small pimples around the hair follicles.The condition can be itchy and sore.

q: A male child presented with swelling in the scalp for 3 months. He has a dog in the home. Diagnosis?
e:
D. Kerion
Explanation
Option A-Folliculitis is a common skin condition that happens when hair follicles become inflamed. It's often caused by an infection with bacteria. At first it may look like small pimples around hair follicles.The condition can be itchy and sore. Option B-A skin abscess is a bump within or below the skin’s surface. It is usually full of pus, painful, and may feel thick and swollen. This is typically caused by a bacterial infection. Option C-Epidermoid cysts are harmless small bumps beneath the skin. They are most common on the face, neck and trunk.Epidermoid cysts are slow growing and often painless, so they rarely cause problems or need treatment. Option D-A kerion is an inflammatory, pus-filled sore (abscess) that sometimes oozes. Kerions form when our immune system overreacts to the fungal infection ringworm (tinea corporis). They most often appear on your scalp, but they may also appear on your face, neck, shoulders and upper arms.The history of dog in the home also suggests diagnosis of fungal infection.

q: A 23 year female, primi gravida, whose nephew is staying in the same house, contracted varicella. Patient had no history of past exposure. She visited medical care centre where the varicella antibody test done and found negative?
o: She is susceptible to chicken pox

q: A patient with the ringworm infection of the scalp. On wood’s lamp examination, dermatophytic infection was suspected. Hair perforation test was positive. diagnosis?

Rubrum.Hair perforation test is positive in cases of T.mentagrophyte. q: Patient on multidrug therapy for leprosy presented with inflammation of the existing lesions, nerve involvement is also seen without systemic features. What will be the treatment approach?

q: Which of the following is used as nail lacquer for fungal infections?

q: Identify the phenomenon shown in the image:
e:
A. Isomorphic phenomenon
Explanation
Option A-The Koebner phenomenon is the appearance of new skin lesions on previously unaffected skin secondary to trauma.This phenomenon is also termed the isomorphic response, given that the new lesions appear clinically and histologically identical to the patient’s underlying cutaneous disease.In other words, a patient with psoriasis who exhibits koebnerization (and is said to be “Koebner-positive”) develops new psoriasiform lesions along sites of skin injury, even if trivial. Option B-The reverse Koebner phenomenon is the disappearance of a skin lesion after trauma to the area. Option C-Gottron papules are symmetric changes over the extensor surfaces of joints, being characterised with erythematous and scaly plaques,seen in dermatomyositis. Option D-Nikolsky sign is demonstrated when lateral pressure is applied on the border of an intact blister, which results in the dislodgment of the normal epidermis and extension of the blister.

q: Identify the condition shown in the image:
e:
A. DLE
Explanation
Option A-The given image depicts DLE,which is characterised by persistent scaly plaques on the scalp, face, and ears which subsequently can progress to scarring and atrophy. Option B-SLE can present with malar rash with sparing of nasolabial folds. Option C-Rosacea is common and is characterised by persistent facial redness. It typically has a relapsing and remitting course, with symptoms controlled by lifestyle measures, general skin care, medications, and procedural interventions. Option D-Vitiligo presents with a hypopigmented patch.

q: Identify the condition
e:
B. Tinea Corporis
Explanation

The sores can develop quickly. Most often they appear on the legs. The exact causes of pyoderma gangrenosum are unknown, but it appears to be a disorder of the immune system. Option D-Ichthyosis vulgaris is an inherited or acquired skin condition that occurs when the skin doesn’t shed its dead skin cells.This causes dry, dead skin cells to accumulate in patches on the surface of the skin. It’s also known as “fish scale disease” because the dead skin accumulates in a similar pattern to a fish’s scales.

q: A 25 year old male presents with grouped vesicles over lips as shown in image. Diagnosis is?

D. Herpes labialis

Bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus and Group A streptococcus cause the infection, which can lead to itchy sores and blisters,which can lead to honey colored crust. Treatment includes antibiotics. Option B-Pemphigus vulgaris presents with a flaccid blister. Option C-Varicella zoster occurs along a dermatomal distribution due to reactivation of virus. q: One-year-old child presents with eczematous dermatitis over face (Image shown). His mother has the history of bronchial asthma. Diagnosis?

D. Atopic dermatitis

It causes dry, itchy skin. It’s a very common condition in babies and children. It usually first appears between ages 3 and 6 months.In babies, symptoms usually affect the face, neck, scalp, elbows, and knees.Also,His mother has the history of bronchial asthma,which supports diagnosis of Atopic dermatitis.

q: A patient presented to the OPD with complaints of papular lesions over the extremities. On examination the lesions were soft and non-tender. Image of the lesion is provided below. What is the probable diagnosis of this case?

D. Common warts

q: Identify the disorder depicted in the image below?
e:
D. Contact leukoderma
Explanation
Option A-Vitiligo causes your skin to lose color or pigmentation. Smooth white or light areas called macules or patches appear on your skin. It generally starts on your hands, forearms, feet and face.But there will be no history of application of any chemical. q: Identify the arthropod shown in image?

B. Sarcoptes scabiei var hominis

q: Tzanck smear is used to diagnose all except?
e:
D. HIV
Explanation

q: A dead body is brought with a ligature mark on the neck. The mark is below the thyroid cartilage, transverse and is completely encircling the neck. No salivary dribbling noted. The condition is ?
e:
C. Ligature strangulation
Explanation
Ligature Strangulation using a rope, belt, or wire, causing a horizontal ligature mark below the thyroid cartilage. Unlike hanging, it completely encircles the neck and lacks salivary dribbling Other options; A) Throttling: Manual strangulation using hands, fingers, or forearm. Typically presents with bruises, nail marks, and petechiae on the neck and face B) Mugging: A form of strangulation where force is applied using a forearm or elbow. Often occurs during a robbery or physical assault D) Hanging: Suspension by a ligature, causing an oblique and incomplete ligature mark above the thyroid cartilage. Salivary dribbling is a key feature seen in antemortem hanging.

q: A 40 year old male has acute loss of hair, specially noticed at lateral part of eyebrow and eyelash. Some behavioral abnormality is noted in him by his wife, who brings him to a doctor. O/E- something on his fingernails is noted. The diagnosis is?
e:
A. Thallium poisoning
Explanation
Thallium Poisoning: Acute hair loss (including lateral eyebrows and eyelashes), neurological symptoms (behavioral changes, paraesthesia), and Mees’ lines (white bands on fingernails) Common sources: Contaminated food, pesticides, rodenticides.

Other options:
B) Arsenic Poisoning causes chronic peripheral neuropathy, hyperpigmentation, and hyperkeratosis. Mees’ lines on nails may be seen but acute hair loss is not a characteristic feature
C) Lead Poisoning causes neurological issues (lead encephalopathy), abdominal pain (lead colic), and basophilic stippling of RBCs. No significant hair loss; mainly affects the nervous and hematologic systems
D) Mercury Poisoning causes tremors, excessive salivation (ptyalism), irritability, and kidney damage. No significant alopecia but may cause acrodynia (pink discoloration of hands/feet in chronic exposure)

q: The enzyme affected in lead poisoning is?
e:
A. Ferochelatase
Explanation
Lead inhibits ferrochelatase, preventing the incorporation of iron into protoporphyrin, leading to increased free protoporphyrin and anemia

Other options:
B) Uroporphyrinogen I synthase is deficient in Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP), not lead poisoning
C) Uroporphyrinogen III synthase deficiency leads to Congenital Erythropoietic Porphyria (Gunther's disease), unrelated to lead poisoning
D) ALA synthase: Rate-limiting enzyme of heme synthesis, but lead does not inhibit it; instead, it inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase

q: A 3 year old child is brought to emergency in comatose condition with history of consumption of iron tablets. He is having abdominal pain and has had diarrhea and vomiting. The treatment is?
e:
C. Desferrioxamine
Explanation
Desferrioxamine: Iron chelator that binds free iron and enhances its excretion via urine. Used in severe iron poisoning with metabolic acidosis, shock, or serum iron levels >500 µg/dL

Other options:
A) BAL (British Anti-Lewisite): Used for arsenic, lead, and mercury poisoning. Not effective for iron poisoning
B) Activated Charcoal: Ineffective for iron poisoning because iron does not bind to charcoal. Mainly used for organic toxins, drugs, and some heavy metals
D) Penicillamine: Used for copper poisoning (Wilson’s disease) and mild cases of lead poisoning

q: The antidote in opioid poisoning is?
