q: A 45-years old man presented to the OPD with dysphagia to both solid and liquids. Esophageal manometry was performed – It revealed premature contraction with > 20% wet swallows and abnormally increased lower esophageal pressure of >450 mm Hg.The diagnosis is-
e:
C. Type 3 achalasia
Explanation
This is a case of Achalasia cardia,which results from damage to nerves in the food tube (oesophagus), preventing the oesophagus from squeezing food into the stomach.The patient will have dysphagia to both solid and liquids. 1. Type I (classical achalasia)-normal pressure. 2. Type II(pan oesophageal pressurisation)-On manometry there will be premature contraction with > 20% wet swallows. 3. Type III (vigorous achalasia) -On manometry there will be premature contraction with > 20% wet swallows and distal spastic contractions as mentioned in question. Option D-Jackhammer esophagus is a specific disorder of the muscular action of the esophagus, wherein there are high amplitude abnormal contractions of the esophageal muscle. These contractions are of much higher force than normal and also are discoordinated compared to normal contraction.

q: A 50 year old female presented with Dysphagia and chest pain. Barium image is given below. What is the most probable diagnosis?
e:
B. DES
Explanation
Option A-Carcinoma esophagus presents as an irregular filling defect. Option B-The given image shows Cork screw appearance,which is seen in DES (diffuse oesophageal spasm). Option C-oesophageal web is seen as a filling defect on barium swallow. Option D-Achalasia cardia is seen as a bird beak appearance.

q: Azygous preserving repair of TEF is done for following reason?
e:
A. Decongest the anastomosis
Explanation
Option A-Azygous preserving repair of TEF is done to Decongest the anastomosis and improve the venous drainage. Option B-In Azygous preserving repair of TEF,surgery becomes little bit tough. Option C- Azygous preserving repair of TEF has nothing to do with recurrence.

q: What is the diagnosis of following Barium X-ray?
e:
B. CA esophagus
Explanation
Option A-Achalasia Cardia is seen as a smooth narrowing in distal oesophagus. Option B-The given image shows irregular narrowing in distal oesophagus,which is s/o CA esophagus. Option C-Plummer Vinson Syndrome is characterised by post-cricoid webs. Option D-GERD can show feline oesophagus on barium.

q: A 4 year old boy presented to casualty by his mother with difficulty in swallowing.He was playing with coins.Chest x-ray is suggestive of following:-
e:
A. Oesophagus foreign body.
Explanation
Option A-The given image shows coin which is seen as a circular object on AP CXR,is s/o Oesophagus foreign body. Option B-Tracheal foreign body will be seen as linear opacity in the midline. Option C-Soft tissue neck calcification won't be so big,round and regular. Option D-Artifact is less likely,since there is history of playing with coins.

q: True about barett’s esophagus are all of the following except?
o: Hyperplastic change in the lining of oesophagus
Histology of the lesion shows mucus secreting goblet cells
Chronic GERD is a predisposing factor
e:
A. Hyperplastic change in the lining of oesophagus
Explanation
Option A-Barett oesophagus is a metaplastic change (not Hyperplastic change) in the lining of oesophagus. Option B-Patient is usually asymptomatic. Option C-Histology of the lesion shows mucus secreting goblet cells due to intestinal metaplasia. Option D-Chronic GERD is a predisposing factor for barett oesophagus.

q: Serpiginous ulcer in distal esophagus is caused by
e:
A. CMV
Explanation
Option A-Serpiginous ulcer in distal esophagus is caused by CMV.CMV also have inclusion bodies-intracytoplasmic (basophilic) and intranuclear (eosinophilic). Option B-Herpes produces small vesicles, they are painful, and when they rupture they form volcano appearance and have inclusion body of Cowdry type-A. Option C,D-Pills and Corrosive do not cause Serpiginous ulcer.

q: 7 week old male child with projectile non- Bilious vomiting. Which electrolyte imbalance can be seen?
e:
A. Hypochloremic Hypokalemic alkalosis
Explanation
This is a case of CHPS (congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis). The child has hypochloremic , hypokalemic, metabolic alkalosis + paradoxical aciduria (due to aldosterone) due to vomiting.

q: Which is fluid of choice for CHPS?
e:
B. 5% Dextrose + 0.45% NACL +20 mg of KCL
Explanation
fluid of choice for CHPS 5% Dextrose + 0.45% NACL +20 mg of KCL. 5% Dextrose-to combat hypoglycemia. 0.45% NACL-to compensate for sodium losses in vomit. 20 mg of KCL-to compensate hypokalemia and hypochloremia.

q: The abdominal mass in pyloric stenosis in a new born child can be best palpated at?
e:
C. In the epigastric area
Explanation
The abdominal mass in pyloric stenosis in a new born child can be best palpated at epigastric area as the thickened pylorus lies in epigastric area.

q: Most common site of gastric ulcer?
e:
A. Lesser curvature at incisura angularis
Explanation
Option A-Most common site of benign gastric ulcer is at lesser curvature at incisura angularis. Option B-Malignant ulcer occurs more towards greater curvature. Option C,D-Fundus and Pyloric antrum are not the most common site of ulcer.

q: Which of the following is an indication of endoscopic treatment in bleeding peptic ulcer?
e:
C. Visible vessel at base
Explanation
based on forest classification (based on endoscopic appearance of ulcer) Type I – bleeding continuing (pulsatile is type IA and oozing is IB) – high risk for rebleed. Type II –evidence of past bleeding a – visible vessel at the base – high risk for rebleed. b – clot at the base c – acid hematin at the base (black) Type III – clean ulcer base. Among the given options,Visible vessel at base is the most important indication of endoscopic treatment in bleeding peptic ulcer.

q: An adult male presented with symptoms of duodenal ulcer. Maximum chances of recurrence with minimal morbidity would be seen after?
e:
D. Gastrojejunostomy
Explanation
Option A-Truncal vagotomy have recurrence rate of < 5% Option B-Highly selective vagotomy have recurrence rate of < 10% Option C-Truncal vagotomy + enterectomy recurrence rate of only 1% (least recurrence rate). Option D-Highest recurrence rate is of gastrojejunostomy (by 50%). It bypasses all the acid into the jejunum so the the acid is gone and ulcers heals but due to high recurrence rate, It is not done anymore for the Treatment of ulcer. It is only done for drainage.

q: In a patient with Carcinoma stomach with GOO, invading in Head of pancreas with metastasis in Right lobe of Liver. Next best treatment is?
e:
A. Palliative Gastrojejunostomy with chemotherapy.
Explanation
Option A-Gastric cancer going to spleen and pancreas is operable But the cancer going to head of pancreas and liver is inoperable. Hence,Palliative Gastrojejunostomy with chemotherapy should be done. Option B-Whipple’s is done for pancreatic primary head cancer. Option C-Radical gastrectomy + right hepatectomy is not done in these cases. Option D-Follow up alone won't be done in these cases.

q: In a patient complaining dyspepsia, upper GI endoscopy and biopsy revealed low grade MALToma. What is the best treatment for this patient?
e:
A. Antibiotics
Explanation
Maltoma is cause by H.pylori. Low grade Maltoma is treated by H.pylori eradication by antibiotics. High grade Maltoma is treated by general CHOP chemotherapy.

q: A patient presented to casualty with complaints of pain abdomen since 4 days, fever and obstruction. X-ray abdomen erect was done as depicted below .What is the possible pathology.
e:
A. Hollow viscus perforation.
Explanation
Option A-The given image shows Gas under diaphragm which clearly indicates Hollow viscus perforation. Option B-Liver abscess usually doesn't have history of obstruction. Option C-Subphrenic abscess with gas forming organisms can have similar presentation,but Hollow viscus perforation is more likely in this case scenario. Option D-Empyema thorax won't cause gas under diaphragm.

q: A patient came to emergency room with severe abdominal pain. Pulse 112 beats/ min and SBP is 80 mmHg. Chest X-ray shown below. What will be the next step of management
e:
B. Resuscitation then exploratory laparotomy
Explanation
Option A-The next step will be resuscitation then exploratory laparotomy. Option B-The patient is having hypotension, tachycardia and gas under diaphragm s/o hollow viscus perforation. The next step will be resuscitation then exploratory laparotomy. Option C-CT scan cannot be done as patient is unstable. Option D-Laparoscopy cannot be done as patient is unstable.

q: False statement regarding duodenal atresia is?
o: Plain X ray shows double bubble sign.
Commonest presenting symptom is bilious vomiting few hours after birth.
e:
C. Obstetrical Ultrasound shows oligohydroamnios (In 50%).
Explanation
Option A-Plain X ray shows double bubble sign in duodenal atresia. Option B-Commonest presenting symptom in duodenal atresia is bilious vomiting few hours after birth. Option C-we don’t see oligohydroamnios,we see Polyhydroamnios as baby won't be able to swallow all the fluid. Option D-Treatment of choice for duodenal atresia is Duodeno-duodenostomy.

q: Most common type of gallstone is
e:
A. Mixed stones
Explanation
Option A-Most common type of gallstone is Mixed Stone. Option B-Most common type of gallstone in west is cholesterol stones. Option C,D-Most common type of gallstone in india is Pigment stone.

q: Type of cholesterol present in gall stones is?
e:
D. Crystalline cholesterol monohydrate
Explanation
Cholesterol present in gall stones is Crystalline cholesterol monohydrate.

q: A 40 years old patient came in emergency department with abdominal colic and features of obstructive jaundice. Her counts and liver enzymes were elevated. A USG was done and gallbladder was scleroatrophic and CBD was impacted with stones along with IHBR dilation. Which is the next step in the management of this patient?
e:
C. ERCP-MRCP
Explanation
When the stone is in the gall bladder, it present as cholecystitis, IOC is USG and T/t is Cholecystectomy. When the stone is in bile duct it presents as Cholangitis which is characterised by pain, fever, jaundice.All three are recurrent. IOC is MRCP and T/t is ERCP.

q: Patient presented with pain in right upper abdomen. MRCP image given below. Next step in the management?
e:
B. ERCP
Explanation
Option A-1st we have to treat CBD stone, so the next step will be ERCP and after few days, we can do cholecystectomy for gall stones. Option B-The given image of MRCP is showing gall stone as well as CBD stone. 1st we have to treat CBD stone, so the next step will be ERCP and after few days, we can do cholecystectomy for gall stones. Option C,D-CECT and PTC is not required as diagnosis is obvious here.

q: 60 year old female with multiple episodes of bilious vomiting and abdominal distention with increased bowel sounds. (X ray abdomen is s/o air fluid levels, Pneumobilia and Features of small bowel obstruction)
e:
A. Gall stone ileus
Explanation
Option A-This is Rigler’s triad of gall stone Ileus. Gall stone Ileus – patient develops a fistula between gall bladder and ileum, and stone comes in the duodenum and this stone passes forward tumbling obstruction or intermittent obstruction, finally goes and get stuck in distal ileum causing small bowel obstruction which is called gall stone ileus. Option B,C,D-Ischemic enterocolitis,GI TB and Adynamic obstruction don't show pneumobilia.

q: False statement about Gall stone ileus is?
o: Usual site of obstruction is Distal ileum.
e:
B. Rigler’s triad is seen in 10-15%
Explanation
Option A-Usual site of obstruction is Distal ileum is a true statement. Option B-Rigler’s triad is seen in 15 – 80% patients and not 10-15%. Option C-Gall stone causes intermittent obstruction is a true statement. Option D-Pneumobilia is an ubiquitous sign of Gall stone ileus.

q: Mascagni node is encountered in which surgery?
e:
D. Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
Explanation
Mascagni node is same as Cystic node of Lund. We get it in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy.

q: In laparoscopic surgery what should be good manipulation angle for good ergonomics?
e:
C. 60 degrees
Explanation
There are 3 angles we should know in Laparoscopic surgery. 1. Elevation Angle – angle b/w operating instrument and table. 60 degrees 2. Manipulation Angle - angle b/w two operating instrument. 60 degrees 3. Azimuth angle - Angle b/w operating camera and scope. 30 degrees

q: Which of the following investigation can not be done after Mini-gastric bypass?
e:
A. ERCP
Explanation
Option A-In Mini-gastric bypass,you will bypass the the initial segment of small intestine where bile duct normally opens,hence,ERCP can't be done. Option B,C,D-MRCP,PTBD and EUS can be done easily in cases of mini gastric bypass.

q: 2 years Post cholecystectomy patients comes with CBD stone. Diagnosis is?
e:
A. Primary CBD stone
Explanation
The bile duct stone can be primary or can be secondary. Primary – which forms inside CBD and Secondary – which comes from gall bladder All most all primary stones are brown pigment stone, all other types comes from gall bladder. Once we have done the cholecystectomy, and later on we find stone in the bile duct, it can be before surgery which was missed or it can be new stone Called Retained and Recurrent stone respectively. The Retained stone is Secondary stone and it presents within <2yrs , Recurrent stone is always Primary and it occurs after >2yrs.

q: Gall bladder cancer at Fundus, infiltrating up to serosa, not going beyond serosa and not involving liver.stage is?
e:
B. T2
Explanation
In gall bladder there is no submucosa and no muscularis mucosae. In mucosa TiS i.e. carcinoma insitu. T/t- cholecystectomy, port site excision not needed now. In lamina propria – T1a, T/t- cholecystectomy In muscularis propria – T1b, T/t – extended cholecystectomy When it reaches upto serosa is T2 (it should not go beyond the serosa, should not breach the serosa), T/t – extended cholecystectomy When it goes outside serosa – T3, T/t – extended cholecystectomy 2 organ involvement/major vessel involvement is T4 (totally inoperable)

q: Which of the following is an example of selective shunt?
e:
A. Sarfeh shunt
Explanation
Option A-Sarfeh shunt is example of selective shunt. Option B,C-Mesocaval shunt and Portocaval shunt is example of partial shunt. Option D-Rex shunt is example of non-selective shunt.

q: Most common site for intra abdominal abscess in relation to liver?
e:
C. Right subhepatic space
Explanation
Between the kidney and the liver, there is Right sub hepatic space called as Morrison pouch. Morrison pouch is the most dependent part when the person is supine. So in relation to liver the Most common site for intra abdominal abscess is Right Subhepatic space.

q: Adult male while eating in a restaurant develops sudden choking.What should be done next?
o: Large sip of water of fizzy drink to push the food bolus down
e:
A. Heimlich manoeuvre
Explanation
Option A-Heimlich manoeuvre – make a clench fist and hold the person from behind at the epigastrium, and give upward and backward 3 forcefull jerks to remove the foreign body from the trachea out. Option B,D-Chest thumping and Blind finger extraction is not done. Option D-When it is mentioned choking, it is in the trachea and not in the esophagus, so drink large sip of water of fizzy drink are of NO USE.

q: Gas-less abdomen is seen in?
e:
B. Acute pancreatitis
Explanation
More appropriate answer will be Tracheo esophageal fistula type A/B. Out of these four the most correct answer is Acute pancreaitis. X-ray features of Acute pancreaitis.– 1. sentinel loop 2. Colon cut off sign 3. Obscured psoas shadow 4. Ground glass appearance of abdomen 5. Gas less abdomen ulcerative colitis shows lead pipe colon. Intussusception shows claw sign on barium enema. Necrotising enterocolitis shows pneumatosis intestinalis.

q: A 40 female presented to surgery casualty with mild Pain abdomen, abdominal distention since 4 days.USG is s/o Peripancreatic fluid collection.whic of the following will be raised ?
e:
A. Serum lipase.
Explanation
Option A-Whenever we have pancreatitis we have fluid around the pancreas in approx. 30-40% patients. The enzyme in pancreatitis that will be raised is Serum lipase. Option B-GGT increase in alcoholic liver disease. Option C,D-BILIRUBIN and CEA are raised in various conditions.

q: Acute pancreatitis with worsening clinical features.CT scan showing infected necrosis, and peri-pancreatic fluid collection.This is best managed by?
e:
D. Percutaneous drainage
Explanation
Option A-Conservative Treatment can't be done as fluid is infected. Option B-Laparoscopic lavage of peritoneum is not done as the 1st step. Option C-Internal drainage can be done in cases of pseudocyst. Option D-It is mentioned that the patient have infected necrosis so we will do Percutaneous drainage. The fluid we can drain but for the necrosis we have to do Necrosectomy.

q: A 8 year old child is brought with well defined mass in epigastrium. He met with an accident 6 weeks back when he fell accidentally and sustained injury in his upper abdomen. What is the most probable cause for this swelling?
e:
C. Pseudocyst of pancreas
Explanation
Option A-Gastric duplication cyst is congenital. Option B-Hemangioma liver is not associated with trauma. Option C-The most probable cause of swelling is Pseudocyst of pancreas.Due to trauma, the duct leaks and the fluid comes out through the duct so now there is a pseudo cyst connected to the duct. Option D-Periumbilical inclusion cyst will not be seen in epigastrium.

q: Most common cause of chronic pancreatitis?
e:
A. Alcohol
Explanation
Most common cause of chronic pancreatitis is Alcohol. Most common cause of acute pancreatitis is gall stone > Alcohol

q: First investigation for a suspected case of cancer head of pancreas is?
e:
B. Endoscopic USG guided FNAC
Explanation
Option A,B-The best way to take a biopsy is Endoscopic USG guided FNAC. And not CT guided biopsy. Option C,D-Laparotomy and MRI guided biopsy is not done.

q: Tumor of the uncinate process of pancreas affects which of the following vessel?
e:
A. Superior mesenteric artery
Explanation
Option A-Tumour of the uncinate process of pancreas affects the Superior mesenteric artery as it passes between head of pancreas and uncinate process. Option B-Portal vein forms behind neck of pancreas. Option C-Common hepatic artery is a branch of celiac trunk. Option D-Inferior Mesenteric artery arises at L3 level.

q: Which is the most common pancreatic endocrine neoplasm?
e:
A. Insulinoma
Explanation
Most common pancreatic cancer – Adenocarcinoma. Most common pancreatic endocrine cancer is Non functional polypeptidoma (asymptomatic) > Insulinoma. Most common malignant/enteropancreatic/MEN-1 pancreatic cancer – Gastrinoma

q: What is the most common site of gastrinoma in MEN1 syndrome?
e:
C. Duodenum
Explanation
Not only in MEN-1,otherwise, also Most common site of gastrinoma is Duodenum(90%).

q: Identify the triangle in the image given below
e:
B. Gastrinoma triangle
Explanation
Option A-Koch's triangle is a triangular anatomical area in the right atrium of the heart, used as a landmark for the atrioventricular (AV) node, and is bounded by the tendon of Todaro, the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve, and the coronary sinus orifice. Option B-This triangle is called Passaro triangle which is the triangle of Gastrinoma. Option C-Sherren’s triangle is for appendicitis. Option D-Hesselbach’s triangle is site for direct inguinal hernia.

q: Patient presents with peritonitis and during surgery diverticular perforation is seen with purulent contamination. What is Hinchey’s stage?
e:
C. 3
Explanation
localized abscess- Hinchey 1 Distant abscess - Hinchey 2 Purulent abscess – Hinchey 3 Feculent abscess - Hinchey – 4

q: Which type of Manoeuvre is shown in the picture?
e:
D. Cattell Braasch maneuver
Explanation
Option A-Kocher’s maneuver is done for mobilisation of duodenum. Option B-Full mobilization of the PDC from the common bile duct to the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) exposes the head of the pancreas, the second and some of the third portions of the duodenum, and the underlying vena cava, the so-called extended Kocher maneuver. Option C-Mattox Maneuver is done for mobilisation of left colon. Option D-When ascending colon is mobilized to approach vena cava in trauma or right kidney this is called Cattell Braasch Maneuver.

q: A child presented with evisceration of bowel loops coming out of a defect in abdominal wall right to the umbilicus. The possible diagnosis is:
e:
C. Gastroschisis
Explanation
Option A-Bowel coming out from umbilicus is omphalocele.It has a sac covering intestine. Option B-Umbilical hernia will be seen coming out from umbilicus. Option C-Defect in wall of abdomen right to the umbilicus is Gastroschisis. It has no sac covering intestines. Option D-Patent urachus will be in midline and there will be no evisceration of intestines.

q: A new born was brought with abdominal distention for 3 days. He has not passed meconium since birth. O/E there is absent anal orifice. What should be the next step in the management of this patient?
e:
D. Cross table X ray
Explanation
Option A,B,C-surgery won't be the next step.First we've to confirm diagnosis. Option D-Next step will be X-Ray. Because if air shadow ends above pubo-coccygeal line it is a high type of ano rectal malformation.If shadow appears below pubo-coccygeal line,it is low type of ano rectal malformation.

q: X ray image. Site of obstruction?
o: Obstruction at the level of Jejunum
e:
B. Ileum
Explanation
Mid ileal obstruction

q: Old frail patient with rectal prolapse and a photo of encircling suture around anus?
e:
A. Thiersch operation
Explanation
A rectal prolapse patient, the surgeon’s finger is inside and he is making a perstring suture to close this i.e. Thiersch operation (not done commonly)

q: A 55 year old male presented with a small peri-anal opening with occasional mild pus discharge. What is the diagnosis?
e:
B. Fistula in Ano
Explanation
By the side of anal wart there is a fistula opening with mild pus discharge i.e. fistula in ano

q: Most commonly used radio-isotope in PET scan is
e:
A. 18 F
Explanation
A small dose of the radio-pharmaceutical agent 18F - fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG). This enters cells and is phosphorylated to FDG 6-phosphate which cannot be metabolized further. Since it is a highly polar molecule , it cannot easily diffuse back out of the cell. After intravenous injection of FDG , it continuously accumulates in the metabolically active cell.

q: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) used in Preoperative staging of Gastro Oesophageal tumours is to detect
e:
A. Distant metastatic disease
Explanation
The main advantage of PET scan is the identification of distant metastasic disease . The disadvantages of PET scans are Radiation burden, high cost .

q: Ureteric bud develops from ?
o: Ureteric bud develops from mesonephric duct
e:
B. Ureteric bud develops from mesonephric duct
Explanation
Ureter develops from mesonephric duct. Wolffian duct develops from mesonephric duct that further forms vas deferns, seminal vesicle and ejaculatory duct.

q: 5 years old girl presented with continuous dribbling, but she is having normal voiding also. What is the most probable diagnosis?
e:
D. Ectopic ureter
Explanation
History is suggestive of she is having one opening of the ureter in the bladder and one in the urethra i.e. Ectopic ureter. When there are 2 ureter on 1 kidney they will always cross.

q: Artery that bleeds during PCNL when the tract is made through column of Bertin is?
e:
A. Interlobar
Explanation
Column of bertin – space b/w the 2 medulla in kidney. When we do PCNL we go through the medulla and remove the stone, if we go through the column of bertin we can damage the Interlobar artery.

q: Which of the following is not a feature of Potter syndrome?
e:
A. Hypospadias
Explanation
Potter syndrome is a feature of renal agenesis due to oligo hydroamnios it will have Pulmonary hypoplasia, Broad flat nose and micrognathia, Limb deformity.

q: Oligohydramnios is found in?
e:
A. Renal agenesis
Explanation
Potter syndrome is a feature of renal agenesis due to oligo hydroamnios it will have Pulmonary hypoplasia, Broad flat nose and micrognathia, Limb deformity.

q: In a case of impalpable testis during laparoscopy the testicular artery was found ending blindly without supplying any tissue. What should be next step in surgery?
o: Explore inguinal canal from outside and do orchidopexy
Stop the procedure and give a course of GnRH
e:
C. No further intervention needed
Explanation
It is agenesis of testis i.e. Anorchia, so no further intervention needed. Best investigation to diagnosis of Anorchia – Laparoscopy

q: All the following statement regarding testicular torsion is true, except?
o: Prompt exploration and fixation is only way to save the testis
U/L fixation should be done immediately
Clapper bell deformity is most common cause
e:
C. U/L fixation should be done immediately
Explanation
B/L fixation is done immediately and not U/L.

q: Patient with suspected PUJ obstruction, best diagnose by?
e:
B. MAG 3 scan
Explanation
MAG 3 scan > DTPA scan DMSA scan is for scarring.

q: False statement about Posterior urethral valve is?
o: This condition is only seen in boys
Most common site in just above veru montanum
May be associated with bladder atony or urinary ascites
e:
C. Most common site in just above veru montanum
Explanation
It is not seen above veru montanum, it is seen below veru montanum.

q: A “70” years old male underwent TURP for BPH. His biopsy revealed a focus of prostatic adenocarcinoma with Gleason score 6. Further best treatment for this patient is?
e:
D. Observation
Explanation
Gleason score <7 and age > 70 yr – observation/ Active surveillance If gleason >7 and age is young than we go for treatment.

q: A 75 year old Male presented to surgery OPD with serum PSA-8.0 ng/dl, with focal mass in prostate, Gleason score of 6. What is next best option for treatment.
e:
C. Active surveillance
Explanation
Gleason score <7 and age > 70 yr – observation/ Active surveillance

q: Carcinoma prostate presented with back pain. On x ray bone metastasis was found in spine. Route of hematogenous spread of prostate cancer to lumbar vertebra?
e:
D. (internal vertebral plexus) BATSON’S PLEXUS
Explanation
(Internal vertebral plexus) BATSON’S PLEXUS which communicates with Peri prostatic plexus Latitude trial: Abiraterone plus Prednisone in Metastatic, Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer

q: RCC involving the adrenals is?
e:
D. Stage IV
Explanation
RCC involving the adrenals is Stage IV Before it was Stage III (now changed) T1 - <7 , <4 – T1a >4 – T1b T2 - >7 T3a – perinephric fat/Renal vein thrombus T3b – I.V.C. below diaphragm T3c - I.V.C. above diaphragm T4 – RCC involving the adrenals

q: In otherwise healthy 40 years old man, management of a RCC 5 cm in size at the lower pole is?
e:
B. Partial nephrectomy
Explanation
RCC 5cm and that to on lower pole, best answer will be partial nephrectomy. It is done when RCC < 4cm or <7 cm at pole.

q: Male patient, hard painless mass in testis . Elevated AFP. Next best step?
e:
B. High inguinal orchiectomy
Explanation
This is testicular tumor. Next step will be High inguinal orchiectomy.

q: For a testicular tumour (NSGCT) of 4cm size a patient underwent high inguinal orchidectomy. Post orchidectomy tumour markers were normal. CT scan showed a 4 mm mass in retroperitoneum. Next step?
e:
A. Active surveillance
Explanation
If the retroperitoneum mass is < 1cm, we go for survillence If the mass is > 1cm than we go for T/t.

q: Resected specimen showing bladder and prostate. Diagnosis?
e:
A. Bladder cancer
Explanation
Bladder with prostate and with foleys catheter i.e. radical cystectomy is done, it is a case of bladder cancer.

q: Electrolyte imbalance seen in ileal conduit urinary diversion is?
e:
C. Hyperchloremic hypokalemic metabolic acidosis
Explanation
When we use stomach we have same what we have in CHPS Hypochloremic hypokalemic alkalosis. When we use jejenum Hperkalemic hypochloremic Acidosis When we use ileum/colon Hypokalemic Hyperchloremic Acidosis Mc we use ileal conduit for diversion.

q: Laxative abuse causes which type of stones in kidney-
e:
A. Ammonium acid urate stones
Explanation
Ammonium urate stones are seen in Laxative abuse & Inflammatory bowel diseases

q: Best treatment for 4 cm calcium oxalate stone in renal pelvis is?
e:
B. PCNL
Explanation
ESWL can be used if the size of the stone is 1.5 cm . If more than this preferred treatment is PCN

q: Identify the Image?
e:
B. Staghorn calculus
Explanation
Staghorn calculus – Phosphate stone seen in infection.

q: A 40 female with sterile pyuria, history of pulmonary tuberculosis in the past. X-ray abdomen, Dx?
e:
B. Renal TB
Explanation
History and image is suggestive of putty kidney which is found in Renal TB.

q: 65 years old male without any medical comorbidity presented with fever, and scrotal swelling. Diagnosis?
e:
C. Fournier’s gangrene
Explanation
Patient is having necrosis of the scrotum i.e. Fournier’s gangrene. It develops synergistic infection Gm +ve and Gm –ve The testis is never removed the tunica albuginea acts as a barrier so testis is always preserved in Fournier’s gangrene.

q: A man was brought to the emergency after meeting with an accident and injured his perineum. He gets an urge to micturate but its unable to pass urine. O/e blood was s/c at the tip of urethra and swelling of penis and scrotum?
e:
B. Bulbar urethra
Explanation
Bulbar Urethra, blood is present at the tip of urethra we suspect urethral injury. RGU > SPC

q: A young male presented to ER with history of fall from bike 2 hrs ago, he is not able to pass urine. Attending doctor observed blood at meatus , next step?
e:

q: A diabetic patient presents with sudden onset perineal pain. O examination, foul smelling discharge, and necrotic tissue as seen in the image is noted. Which of the following is true about the given condition?

Urinary diversion is the next step

Management includes iv fluids, iv antibiotics, and urgent surgical excision followed by skin grafting in later stages.

q: Which of the following is the most common complication following ligation of the first vessel during abdominoperineal resection for rectal carcinoma?

q: A 45 year old male underwent bilateral laparoscopic hernia repair for inguinal hernia. Postoperatively, he complained of pain in the right thigh. Which of the following nerve entrapment leads to this symptom?

q: A patient presented with fever and abdominal pain with jaundice. Investigations showed the given findings. Which of the following statements is true regarding his condition?
o: Angioembolization is the treatment of choice
Echinococcus species is involved in etiology
e:
D. Echinococcus species is involved in etiology
Explanation
Echinococcus species is involved in etiology The given CT image shows a cyst in the liver with serpentine linear membranes seen as wavy membranes within the cyst is suggestive of hydatid disease. Hydatid cyst is a zoonotic disease caused by Echinococcus species of flatworms. Its life cycle consists of dogs as definitive hosts and humans as aberrant intermediate hosts. Primary hydatid cysts most commonly occur in the liver. The initial investigation is USG, and a CT scan can be used to diagnose the condition.

q: A 40 year old male patient presents with a swelling that has been slowly growing in the past 2 years. On examination, it was variable in consistency and fully mobile. What is the most likely diagnosis?

B. Parotid tumor
Explanation
Parotid tumor The given clinical scenario and image likely depict a case of parotid tumor, likely to be a pleomorphic adenoma. Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary gland tumor. The most commonly affected gland is the parotid gland.

q: A patient who is a known case of alcohol dependence syndrome presents with sudden and unintentional weight loss. What is the most likely diagnosis? ALP- 240IU/L S. direct bilirubin- 1mg/dl AST/ALT- 0.5 Alpha fetoprotein- 600ng/ml

C. Hepatocellular carcinoma
Explanation
Hepatocellular carcinoma HCC is the most common cause of primary liver cancer. It is more commonly seen in males, at around 65-70 years. The main risk factor for HCC is cirrhosis and Hepatitis B or C, alcohol abuse, metabolic syndrome, or hemochromatosis.

q: A patient presented with features of chronic pancreatitis with recurrent attacks and has a 10mm dilatation of the pancreatic duct with intraductal calculi present. Which of the following is the surgery of choice?

B. Longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy
Explanation
Longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy In this case of chronic pancreatitis with recurrent attacks, 10mm dilatation of the pancreatic duct, and intraductal calculi, longitudinal pacreaticojejunostomy (also known as Puestow procedure or lateral pacreaticojejunostomy) is the surgery of choice.

q: A woman presented with BIRADS-5 breast lesion. Which of the following is a good prognostic factor for this lesion?
e:
C. ER positive
Explanation
ER positive ER positivity is a good prognostic factor in breast cancer. The ER and PR are two steroid hormone receptors present in breast cancers. The expression of these recetors indicates a favorable prognosis and response to hormonal therapy.

q: A patient presents with sudden onset of chest pain shooting to the neck and interscapular region. X-ray shows a widenend mediastinum. BP is 110/90mmHg in the right upper limb and 160/100 in the left upper limb. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
C. Acute aortic dissection
Explanation
Acute aortic dissection Sudden onset severe chest pain, with wide discrepancy in blood pressure between the two limbs, and a widened mediastinum on xray point towards a diagnosis of aortic dissection. It is initiated by an intimal tear, which allows blood to penetrate into the medial layer, producing a false lumen between the inner two thirds and outer one third of the media.

q: A patient presented with right hypochondriac pain. He had an episode of diarrhea 1 week prior. CT scan of the abdomen reveals a liver abscess of around 25ccs. What is the next step in management?
e:
C. Medical therapy
Explanation
Medical therapy The patient most likely has an amoebic liver abscess. The initial treatment of choice for an amoebic liver abscess is medical therapy with metronidazole. Ingestion of Entamoeba histolytica cysts causes intestinal diseases like diarrhea. Following this, the trophozoites reach the liver mostly through the portal venous system and cause amoebic liver abscess. The common presenting features are right upper quadrant pain, tenderness, fever, hepatomegaly, and diarrhea.

q: A 50 year old patient with a history of trauma one week back presents with confusion and ataxia. He is on treatment for alcohol dependence and his last intake was 2 weeks back. CT scan reveals the following finding. What is the diagnosis?
e:
B. Subdural hemorrhage
Explanation
Subdural hemorrhage The given clinical scenario and the plain CT showing a concavo-convex shaped hematoma on the left side with a midline shift to the right is suggestive of subdural hematoma (SDH). An acute SDH is the result of the accumulation of blood between the arachnoid membrane and the dura. It is usually due to the rupture of bridging veins running from the cerebral cortex to the dural sinuses. Elderly and alcoholic patients are at higher risk of acute SDH formation after head trauma due to brain atrophy.

q: Which of the following is false about the given condition?

Hyperbaric oxygen has no role in the treatment of this condition

Explanation
Hyperbaric oxygen has no role in the treatment of this condition The given condition is likely that of Melaney’s gangrene. Melaney’s gangrene is necrotizing fasciitis of the abdominal wall. Hyperbaric oxygen has been shown to reduce mortality in patients with Melaney’s gangrene and therefore plays a significant role in the management of this condition.

q: A patient presents with swelling in the groin region and it is diagnosed as a direct inguinal hernia. Weakness in which of the following structures is most likely to cause this condition?

B. Conjoint tendon
Explanation
Conjoint tendon A direct inguinal hernia is caused due to weakness in the conjoint tendon. Direct inguinal hernia is common in elderly patients. It is seen medial to the inferior epigastric vessels, in Hesselbach’s triangle. This area lacks muscle and contains only fascia.

q: A patient presents with sudden onset of hematemesis. He has been taking aspirin for his arthritis and drinks alcohol occasionally. He gives a history of occasional abdominal pain. On examination, there is no abdominal mass or tenderness. What is the likely diagnosis?
e:
C. Peptic ulcer
Explanation
Peptic ulcer Peptic ulcer disease accounts for around 2/3rd of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The major causative factors are Helicobacter pylori and NSAIDs. Prostaglandins protect gastric and duodenal mucosa from acid and pepsin.

q: A construction worker came to the OPD complaining of white fingers. He has been working in the cement and concrete industry and has been working on heavy machinery drills, wood, and furniture polishing for 20 years. What is the most likely etiology for this condition?
o: Candidal infection of the fingers due to continuous exposure to water
Continuous exposure to cement and concrete
Continuous exposure to drills and machines
e:
D. Continuous exposure to drills and machines
Explanation
Continuous exposure to drills and machines The clinical scenario suggests the diagnosis of Raynayd’s syndrome due to chronic exposure to drills and machines (vibrating tools). Raynauds syndrome occurs due to peripheral vasospasm, and it is more common in the upper extremities. It can occur due to exposure to various stimuli, including cold temperatures, emotional stress, those who use vibrating tools, etc.

q: A 25 year old child was admitted to the hospital for prolapsing rectal mass and painless rectal bleeding. Histopathological examination reveals enlarged and inflamed glands filled with mucin. What is the likely diagnosis?
e:
C. Hamartoma
Explanation
Hamartoma The given features are suggestive of a juvenile polyp, which are a type of hamartomatous polyp. They are benign growths that are composed of a disorganised mixture of different types of tissues. Juvenile polyps are malformations of epithelium and lamina propria commonly located in the rectum. It is seen in children <5 years of age. The typical presentation is painless rectal bleeding. Sometimes, there may be a proliferating rectal mass.

q: Identify the given condition-
e:
D. Trophic ulcer
Explanation
Trophic ulcer The given picture showing an ulcer with punched out edges over a pressure point is most likely that of a trophic ulcer/neuropathic ulcer. q: A 4 year old child presents with easy fatiguability. The mother complains that the child has increased hunger between meals, which is relieved after food. Liver examination revealed no glycogen. The enzyme likely to be deficient is?

A deficiency of glycogen synthase leads to glycogen storage disorder and presents in infancy with early morning drowsiness and fatigue, fasting hypoglycemia, pallor, emesis, and hypoglycemic convulsions. It leads to a marked decrease in liver glycogen stores. Hepatomegaly is absent.

q: A chronic alcoholic patient is diagnosed with gouty arthritis. What biochemical changes will be seen in this patient?
e:
C. Increased urate and lactate levels
Explanation
Increased urate and lactate levels The oxidation of ethanol to acetate by alcohol dehydrogenase is accompanied by reduction of NAD+ to NADH. This results in accumulation of NADH, and increased NADH/NAD+ ratio. There is an increased conversion of pyruvate to lactate causing hyperlacticacidemia which leads to increased renal reabsorption of urate and decreased excretion of uric acid, causing agitation of gouty arthritis.

q: Nerve injured in frey’s syndrome is
e:
A. Auriculotemporal nerve
Explanation
Frey syndrome usually occurs with auriculotemporal nerve injury caused by surgical intervention or trauma in the parotid region, The auriculotemporal nerve, a branch of the trigeminal nerve, consists of parasympathetic fibers that signal the parotid gland to produce saliva and sympathetic fibers that innervate the sweat glands of the face and scalp. When an insult to the parasympathetic and sympathetic nerve fibers of the auriculotemporal nerve in the parotid region occurs, the resulting aberrant regeneration of post-ganglionic parasympathetic nerve fibers (responsible for salivary secretion) along the pre-existing sympathetic pathways to the vessels and sweat glands of the skin leads to the development of Frey syndrome. Patients with Frey syndrome often present with facial warmth, flushing, and sweating in the territory of the auriculotemporal nerve overlying the parotid gland, which may include the preauricular skin, the temporal skin, the scalp, and the temporomandibular joint region. Symptoms occur during meals, especially with spicy and sour foods.

q: An absent gag reflex can result from injury to which of the following nerves?

Explanation
The gag reflex is a reflex contraction of the back of the throat, elicited by touching the posterior pharyngeal wall, tonsillar area, or the base of the tongue. Stimulation results in a visible contraction of the pharyngeal wall. The gag reflex is a protective response that prevents oral contents from entering the throat except as part of normal swallowing and helps prevent choking. The afferent limb of the reflex is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve (cranial nerve IX), which inputs to the nucleus solitarius and the spinal trigeminal nucleus. The efferent limb is supplied by the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) from the nucleus ambiguus. All of these are located in the medulla. The lower cranial nerves are involved in pharyngeal and laryngeal function as well as in movements of the neck and tongue. Damage to them can result in problems with speech and swallowing.

q: A patient with altered sensorium was found to have irregularly irregular pulse with pulse deficit of 20.JVP will show
e:
B. Absent a wave

Myasthenia gravis – Antibody against NMJ receptor

q: In multiple sclerosis, slow conduction of motor and sensory pathway is due to:

Multiple sclerosis, It is a demyelinating disorder.

Motor speech Explanation: Inferior frontal gyrus on the left side gives brocas area. Brocas area is associated with word formation i.e. motor speech.

e:

Explanation

The patient will have fluent speech because the brocas area is not affected. Conduction aphasia – Arcuate fibres are affected. Nominal aphasia – lesion is in the angular gyrus.

q: Defect in dystrophin is characteristic of

Explanation: dystrophin is subsarcolemal protein which is imp. For muscle strength. If this protein is lost the patient will have muscle necrosis and atrophy • DMD is a muscular dystrophy characterized by defect in dystrophin leading to infiltration of muscle by fatty and fibrous tissue.

q: A Patient with History of RTA presented to the OPD after 3 days. CT showed the presence of an SDH. On fundoscopy B/L papilledema was seen. What is the most probable course of this:

q: A 74-year-old male patient was brought to the OPD by his daughter complaining of urinary incontinence and ataxia. On examination he has difficulty in calculating simple arithmetic sums and memory loss. What is the probable diagnosis?

Explanation

q: Cell most affected in multiple sclerosis

Explanation: most commonly affected cell in multiple sclerosis are oligodendrocyte because the myelin sheath formation happens by the oligodendrocytes in the CNS.

q: While performing a lumbar puncture which layer is punctured last

Explanation

The Lumbar Puncture needle pierces in order: skin, subcutaneous tissue, supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space containing the internal vertebral venous plexus, dura, arachnoid, and finally the subarachnoid space.

q: Patient of ptosis, speech disturbance and progressive weakness in body. Symptoms improved on rest. What is the diagnosis?

Explanation: only male dominant polyarthritis is Ankylosing Spondylitis.

q: A patient with hyperkalemia and elevated urea levels underwent dialysis. Towards the end of the session, she became drowsy and had a sudden seizure episode. On examination, the patient was hypotensive. What is the treatment for this condition.
e:
D. IV Mannitol
Explanation
IV Mannitol The given scenario is suggestive of the dialysis disequilbrium syndrome (DDS) or the reverse urea effect. It is an acute complication that occurs especially in patients undergoing dialysis for the first time. DDS can be prevented by: • Slow hemodialysis • Limiting the clearance of urea to prevent the development of an osmotic gradient • Increasing dialysate sodium level • Administration of osmotically active substance

q: A female patient presents with severe restlessness, palpitations, and tremors to the emergency department. She is a known case of bronchial asthma. On examination, the neck looks swollen. Explanation
Diltiazem The given clinical scenario suggests the diagnosis of thyroid storm/thyroid crisis presenting with atrial fibrillation, and the immediate management in this patient is to rate control the arrhythmia with diltiazem (calcium channel blocker).

q: A 25-year-old male patient came with complaints of palpitations, sweating, and restlessness. He has a complaint of sweaty palms. Clinical findings are depicted in the image given below. What is the diagnostic finding seen in this patient?
e:
C. Thyroid receptor antibody
Explanation
Thyroid receptor antibody Based on the clinical findings, the most likely diagnosis is Graves’ disease. Elevated levels of thyroid receptor-stimulating antibodies is diagnostic of Graves disease. The hyperthyroidism of Graves’ disease is caused by thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) that are synthesised in the thyroid gland as well as in bone marrow and lymph nodes.

q: A 50-year-old HIV patient presented with a painful lesion, as shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
B. Kaposi sarcoma
Explanation
Kaposi sarcoma The above image showing a violaceous growth on the hard palate in an HIV patient is diagnostic of Kaposi sarcoma. Kaposi sarcoma is a vascular neoplasm caused by human herpesvirus 8 (HHV 8) and is very common in patients suffering from AIDs. KS is considered to be an AIDS-defining disease.

q: A patient is brought to the OPD by his wife complaining about difficulty in expressing emotions and not taking part in daily activities. On examination, resting tremors and rigidity are noted. Given the possible diagnosis, which part of the brain is affected in this patient?
e:
A. Basal ganglia
Explanation
Basal ganglia Based on the clinical findings given above, the most likely diagnosis is Parkinson’s disease and it is due to degeneration of the substantia nigra in the basal ganglia. It is characterised by resting tremors, rigidity, akinesia, bradykinesia, postural instability, dysphagia, etc.

q: A 45 year old HIV-positive male came with complaints of persistent cough and weight loss. He has skin lesions that appear as umbilicated papules and nodules predominantly on the face, trunk, and upper extremities. Chest x-ray showed multiple bilateral nodular infiltrates. His sputum CBNAAT for tuberculosis was negative and he has a low CD4 count. What is the probable diagnosis?
e:
A. HIV with disseminated histoplasmosis
Explanation
HIV with disseminated histoplasmosis Progressive disseminated histoplasmosis (PDH) is seen in immunocompromised patients. Common risk factors are AIDS, extremes of age, immunosuppressive drugs, etc. It most commonly involves the lungs and bone marrow.

q: A male patient presented to the emergency room with seizures. He has a history of fever, headache, and confusion. An MRI brain was done, and it showed inflammation involving the bitemporal lobe. What is the most likely etiology for this presentation?
e:
C. Herpes simplex virus
Explanation
Herpes simplex virus The given clinical vignette suggests the diagnosis of encephalitis caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). HSV encephalitis is defined as inflammation of brain parenchyma caused by the Herpes virus and it typically presents as an acute febrile illness.

q: A male patient presents with sensory loss and weakness of limbs for 3 months. He also has angular stomatitis. On examination, there is loss of proprioception, vibration sensations, UMN type of lower limb weakness, and absent ankle reflex. What is the most probable diagnosis?
e:
D. Subacute combined degeneration of cord
Explanation
Subacute combined degeneration of cord The given case scenario is suggestive of Subacute combined degeneration of cord (SACD) due to vitamin B12 deficiency. Patients with SACD present with the following features: • Loss of vibration sense and proprioception • Paresthesia • Loss of deep tendon reflexes

q: A 40-year-old female patient came with complaints of chest pain, palpitations, and shortness of breath. On examination, a mid-diastolic murmur was heard, and a prominent ‘a’ wave was found on JVP. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
B. Tricuspid stenosis
Explanation
Tricuspid stenosis The presence of a mid-diastolic murmur and a prominent a-wave in JVP is suggestive of tricuspid stenosis. Mid-diastolic murmurs result from obstruction and/or augmented flow at the level of the mitral or tricuspid valve. Thus both MS and TS present with a mid-diastolic murmur. However, the presence of a prominent a-wave in JVP points towards tricuspid stenosis.

q: A patient who is a known case of hypertension on multiple anti-hypertensive medications came to OPD. His ECG finding is given below. Which of the below drugs is responsible for the ECG finding?
e:
D. Spironolactone
Explanation
Spironolactone Based on the ECG findings (tall T waves), the most likely diagnosis is hyperkalemia, and among the given drugs, spironolactone is the drug that is most likely to cause hyperkalemia. Spironolactone is a potassium sparing diuretic. It is a competitive inhibitor of the mineralocorticoid receptors in the late distal tubule and collecting duct. It causes a decrease in sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the distal tubule, hence it promotes sodium diuresis but maintains body potassium levels.

q: A 78 year old woman presents with a progressive decline in daily activities. She gives a history of convulsions and visual hallucinations. She does not talk to anyone and keeps looking at the sky. Pathology examination shows the presence of Lewy bodies within the neurons. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
A. Parkinson’s disease
Explanation
Parkinson’s disease Parkinson’s disease is due to widespread degeneration of the portion of the substantia nigra that sends dopamine-secreting nerve fibres to the caudate nucleus and putamen. On pathological examination, protein inclusions called Lewy bodies that stain for alpha synuclein are seen.

DDAVP supplements for lifelong Based on the given clinical vignette, the most likely diagnosis is central diabetes insipidus. Lifelong supplementation of desmopressin (DDAVP) is the definitive management in this scenario.

q: A 65 year old chronic smoker came to the medicine OPD with complaints of upper chest discomfort and drooping of an eyelid. He also complained of pain radiating to the upper arm and a tingling sensation in the 4th and 5th digits of his left hand. The chest x-ray is given below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
A. Pancoast tumor
Explanation
Pancoast tumor Pancoast tumor results from a local extension of a tumor growing in the apex of the lung, with involvement of C8, T1 and T2 nerve roots. It presents with pain that radiates to the ulnar distribution of the arm often with destruction of the 1st and 2nd ribs.

q: A chronic alcoholic patient presents with acute pain and swelling of the left great toe. There is no history of trauma. Synovial fluid analysis shows raised leukocytes. Lab investigations show normal serum uric acid levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e:
B. Acute gout
Explanation
Acute gout Gout is a hyperuricemic condition manifested as episodic inflammatory arthritis due to crystal formation and deposition of Monosodium urate (MSU) crystals within the joints and connective tissue. Serum uric acid is usually elevated in chronic gout patients, but it may remain normal or low during acute attacks because of the uricosuric property of inflammatory cytokines.
